work_items.title: Publish NewOrderOffered on Assign + Reassign (after commit, expiresAt = AssignedAt + OfferTimeoutSeconds)
work_items.goal: OrderService.TransitionAsync publishes NewOrderOffered(orderDto, expiresAt) to the offered driver on both Assign and Reassign, after commit alongside OrderChanged. expiresAt = order.AssignedAt + fleet OfferTimeoutSeconds (default 45) — the identical value OfferTimeoutJob reads, so the driver countdown and the server timeout are the same instant. Corrects the stale IRealtimePublisher XML comment.
acceptance_criteria: After the post-commit OrderChangedAsync in OrderService.TransitionAsync, when transition is Assign or Reassign AND order.DriverId is non-null, the service loads OfferTimeoutSeconds for order.FleetId via the (int?)-cast subquery with ?? 45 fallback (the mandatory pattern documented in CLAUDE.md for OfferTimeoutJob — without the (int?) cast a fleet with no FleetSettings row silently gets 0 s), computes expiresAt = order.AssignedAt.Value.AddSeconds(timeout), and calls publisher.NewOrderOfferedAsync(order, order.DriverId.Value, expiresAt, ct).

expiresAt on both Assign and Reassign equals AssignedAt + timeout; ApplyAssign and ApplyReassign both set AssignedAt = now (verified OrderStateMachine.cs 130/226), so a reassigned order gets a fresh, consistent window and never times out early in OfferTimeoutJob.
No NewOrderOffered publish occurs for any transition other than Assign/Reassign, and none when DriverId is null.
The IRealtimePublisher.NewOrderOfferedAsync XML doc comment that claims 'OrderService does NOT call this' is corrected to reflect that OrderService now publishes it on Assign/Reassign.

Assign_PublishesNewOrderOffered_WithDriverAndExpiresAt, Reassign_PublishesNewOrderOffered_ToNewDriver_WithRefreshedExpiresAt, Assign_ExpiresAt_EqualsAssignedAtPlusFleetTimeout, Assign_NoFleetSettingsRow_UsesDefault45, and Accept_DoesNotPublishNewOrderOffered pass (RecordingRealtimePublisher records the call).

work_items.title: X-Idempotency-Key on driver transitions + IdempotencyRecord entity + AddIdempotencyRecords migration
work_items.goal: Optional X-Idempotency-Key header on the six driver transitions (accept/decline/arrive/start/complete/cancel). Same key within 24h replays the stored status+body without re-executing; concurrent duplicate executes once via a unique-index (UserId,Key) claim. Implemented as an endpoint-level helper in Common/Idempotency (no FastEndpoints pre/post-processor precedent exists). IdempotencyRecord is NOT a tenant entity (UserId-scoped, mirrors RefreshToken/SmsCode).
acceptance_criteria: IdempotencyRecord entity: Id (Guid PK), UserId (Guid), Key (string, max 200), RequestHash (string, SHA-256 hex of method+path+body), ResponseStatus (int?), ResponseBody (JsonDocument? mapped .HasColumnType("jsonb") per the OrderEvent.Payload precedent), CreatedAt (DateTimeOffset). It is NOT ITenantEntity and gets NO global query filter (UserId-scoped, mirrors decisions.md assumption 4 for RefreshToken/SmsCode); DbSet<IdempotencyRecord> registered on TaxiDbContext. Configuration adds a unique index on (UserId, Key). Migration AddIdempotencyRecords added with dotnet ef --output-dir Infrastructure/Migrations (CLAUDE.md).
No X-Idempotency-Key header -> the endpoint executes the transition normally and writes no record.

Header present -> IdempotencyHelper computes RequestHash and INSERTs a claim row (ResponseStatus/ResponseBody null) with SaveChanges BEFORE executing; on success it owns the lock, executes the transition, captures status+body, UPDATEs the row, then Sends.

Unique-index violation on the claim INSERT (PostgresException SqlState 23505 via the .ThrowAsync/.Which pattern in CLAUDE.md) -> load the existing row: (a) stored response present -> replay stored ResponseStatus+ResponseBody verbatim, no re-execution; (b) response null and CreatedAt within 60 s -> 409 Idempotency.InFlight (retryable); (c) response null and CreatedAt older than 60 s (crash between claim and store) -> take over, re-execute, store, Send; (d) RequestHash differs -> 409 Idempotency.KeyReused.
Only 2xx and expected terminal 4xx/409 responses are stored; a 5xx (infra failure) is never stored so a retry re-executes. Key longer than 200 chars -> 400 Idempotency.KeyTooLong.
Opportunistic purge DELETE WHERE CreatedAt < now - 24h runs on the claim path (bounded, no new job); 24 h replay window.

Replay_SameKeyWithinWindow_ReturnsStoredResponse_NoReExecution, Concurrent_DuplicateKey_ExecutesOnce_LoserGets409InFlight, OrphanedClaim_OlderThan60s_IsTakenOverAndReExecuted, SameKey_DifferentRequestHash_Returns409KeyReused, NoHeader_ExecutesNormally_WritesNoRecord, FiveHundred_IsNotStored_RetryReExecutes, IdempotencyRecords_TenantGuardBypassed_NoQueryFilter, and KeyTooLong_Returns400 pass (integration, real Postgres).

work_items.title: GET drivers/me/summary + GET drivers/me/orders (DriverOnly, own-rows, tenant-safe) + ActiveOrderId on drivers/me
work_items.goal: Two DriverOnly, driver-scoped, tenant-safe AsNoTracking projection endpoints: summary (rides count, per-payment-type CZK totals, hours online from shifts incl. open shift) for Home chips, and orders (own completed+active rides for the day) for the History list. Also adds ActiveOrderId (additive) to GET drivers/me so B-ride's AC #6 restore has an authoritative source.
acceptance_criteria: GET /drivers/me/summary?date= is DriverOnly, resolves the driver via the sub claim (as GetMeEndpoint does), and returns an AsNoTracking projection { ridesCount, cashTotalCzk, cardTotalCzk, invoiceTotalCzk, hoursOnline } scoped to own rows (DriverId == myDriverId). ridesCount = own Completed orders in the day window; totals sum FinalPriceCzk grouped by PaymentType (integer CZK); hoursOnline sums overlapping DriverShift durations (EndedAt ?? now) - StartedAt clamped to the window, including the open shift.

GET /drivers/me/orders?date= is DriverOnly, own-rows, and returns a read-only list DTO { id, publicCode, status, pickupAddress, dropoffAddress, priceType, finalPriceCzk, paymentType, completedAt } of the driver's own completed AND active rides for the day.

The date query param is bound as string? and parsed with DateOnly.TryParseExact("yyyy-MM-dd", InvariantCulture) to avoid the FastEndpoints locale binding landmine (CLAUDE.md); absent/invalid date -> today (Europe/Prague) interpreted as a UTC [start,end) window. Invalid date format -> 400 via validator.
GET /drivers/me gains ActiveOrderId (Guid?, additive, XML-documented) = the driver's non-terminal order id (Assigned/Accepted/Arrived/InProgress) or null; existing GetMeResponse fields unchanged.
Both summary and orders are tenant-safe via the query filter and never leak another driver's or another fleet's rows.

Summary_CountsOwnCompletedRides_AndTotalsPerPaymentType, Summary_HoursOnline_IncludesOpenShift, Summary_DriverB_CannotSeeDriverAsRides (driver isolation), Summary_CrossTenant_ReturnsOwnFleetOnly (tenant isolation), Orders_ListsOwnCompletedAndActiveRidesForDate, GetMe_ReturnsActiveOrderId_WhenRideInProgress, and Summary_InvalidDate_Returns400 pass.

Must NOT break /x or the dispatcher E2E (devOptions.enabled false so the SW never registers under npm run dev).

work_items.title: Driver login /d/login + silent refresh (single-flight) + IndexedDB refresh token + role landing
work_items.goal: /d/login reusing POST /auth/staff/login with role-based landing (Driver -> /d, else /x). 'Zustat prihlasen' persists the refresh token to IndexedDB. Silent refresh (proactive timer at exp-2min + single-flight 401-retry) added ADDITIVELY to the shared client.ts so a driver is never logged out mid-shift; /x keeps its current clear+redirect path (guarded).
acceptance_criteria: /d/login reuses POST /auth/staff/login (fleet slug + email + password, Czech errors, never JSON/stack trace); on success a Driver role lands on /d and any other role lands on /x.
When 'Zustat prihlasen' is checked the refresh token is persisted to IndexedDB (survives tab kill and phone restart) via idbAuthStore; the access token stays where UC-002 keeps it.

Silent refresh is added additively to client.ts: a proactive timer fires at exp-2min; a 401 triggers exactly ONE shared refresh via a module-level single-flight mutex (two concurrent 401s -> one /auth/refresh call, because refresh rotates tokens and concurrent refreshes would mutually invalidate and log the driver out — the exact failure the spec forbids), then the original request is retried once; only a failed refresh clears storage and routes to /d/login. The existing /x clear+redirect behaviour is unchanged (guarded).

AC #8 (cs/en) parity green; refresh.test.ts proves two concurrent 401s cause exactly one refresh (single-flight) and the proactive timer fires once, idbAuthStore.test.ts (persist/restore/clear via fake-indexeddb) passes, and a testing-library test (bad creds -> Czech error; driver role -> /d) passes.

work_items.title: Full-screen offer takeover: sound/vibration/countdown/double-tap guard + NewOrderOffered handler
work_items.goal: On NewOrderOffered (existing single /hubs/fleet connection, positional (dto, expiresAt)) a full-screen takeover: repeating loud sound + vibration respecting per-driver 'Tichy rezim' (default OFF), large pickup, distance/ETA via geo/route (A-geo), price badge (PEVNA green / Odhad grey / Taxametr), countdown ring to expiresAt, Prijmout (64px) / Odmitnout with reason, double-tap guard (single request), expiry auto-dismiss. Accept/decline are live-only.
acceptance_criteria: The existing NewOrderOffered no-op handler in useFleetHub.ts is extended to render the full-screen takeover from the positional (dto, expiresAt) payload on the single /hubs/fleet connection (the driver auto-joins driver:{driverId}; there is no separate /hubs/driver).
Repeating loud sound + vibration play until answered or expired, feature-detected and no-op in tests, and are suppressed when the per-driver 'Tichy rezim' setting is on (default OFF).

The screen shows large pickup, distance/ETA from GET /geo/route (A-geo), a price badge (PEVNA green / Odhad grey / Taxametr), and a countdown ring driven by expiresAt; when the countdown reaches zero the offer auto-dismisses.

Prijmout is a 64px button issuing POST /orders/{id}/accept; a double-tap issues only ONE request (double-tap guard). Odmitnout requires selecting a reason (Daleko / Mam pauzu / Jiny duvod) -> POST /orders/{id}/decline. When offline, accept/decline are blocked with 'Bez pripojeni, zkuste znovu' (never queued).

AC #8 parity green; offerCountdown.test.ts (fake timers: ring value from expiresAt, auto-dismiss at 0), priceBadge.test.ts (Fixed/Estimate/Meter -> label+colour), and testing-library tests (double-tap -> one request; decline blocked without a reason) pass.

work_items.title: Active ride /d/ride: status button + 5-min no-show timer + nav handoff + map strip + state restore
work_items.goal: Status-driven big button (Accepted: 'Navigovat' + 'Jsem na miste'; Arrived: 'Zahajit jizdu' + 'Zakaznik neprisel' enabled only after a 5-min timer; InProgress: 'Navigovat k cili' + 'Ukoncit jizdu'), tap-to-call phone, collapsible Leaflet map strip, and state restore from IndexedDB + reconcile with GET /drivers/me (ActiveOrderId, A-me) + GET /orders/{id} on load (AC #6).
acceptance_criteria: The big button maps order status to actions: Accepted -> 'Navigovat' (nav handoff) + 'Jsem na miste' (arrive); Arrived -> 'Zahajit jizdu' (start) + secondary 'Zakaznik neprisel' (no-show cancel) enabled ONLY after a visible 5-min timer; InProgress -> 'Navigovat k cili' (if dropoff known) + 'Ukoncit jizdu' (to complete).

Customer phone is tap-to-call; a collapsible Leaflet map strip shows own position + pickup/dropoff pins; nav handoff opens Google Maps / Mapy.cz / Waze via geo: and universal links per the settings preference.

On load the ride state is restored from IndexedDB then reconciled: GET /drivers/me (ActiveOrderId, A-me) is authoritative; if ActiveOrderId is set, GET /orders/{id} supplies the current status (AC #6). If IndexedDB is empty but ActiveOrderId is set, the ride is rebuilt from the server; if the server reports a terminal status, the ride is cleared and the driver returns Home.
arrive/start transitions are issued through the offline queue (B-queue); a transition 409 refetches the order.

AC #8 parity green; rideButtonState.test.ts (status -> button set), noShowTimer.test.ts (fake timers: disabled < 5 min, enabled >= 5 min), navLinks.test.ts (link per nav-app preference + platform), and useRideRestore.test.ts (IndexedDB + ActiveOrderId reconcile precedence) pass.

work_items.title: Background position reporting: watchPosition -> UpdatePosition throttle (3s/25m) + wake lock + 60s banner
work_items.goal: While online, watchPosition (high accuracy) -> hub UpdatePosition every 3s OR when moved > 25m (client throttle; server also throttles), heading+speed included; Wake Lock on ride screens (feature-detected); red 'Poloha se neodesila' banner + single vibration when nothing sent for 60s; degradation notes measured to docs/driver-pwa-limits.md.
acceptance_criteria: While the driver is online, navigator.geolocation.watchPosition (enableHighAccuracy) drives hub UpdatePosition(lat,lng,heading,speed) on the existing /hubs/fleet connection at most every 3s OR when moved > 25m, whichever first; heading and speed are forwarded.

If nothing was sent for 60s while online, a red 'Poloha se neodesila' banner shows and the phone vibrates once; docs/driver-pwa-limits.md records measured Android Chrome / iOS Safari background behaviour.
Vitest strategy: fake timers + mocked navigator.geolocation.watchPosition (injected fake position stream) + a spy on the hub invoke; Wake Lock no-ops when unavailable.

AC #8 parity green; positionThrottle.test.ts (3s tick; 25m displacement triggers early; both boundaries) and usePositionReporting.test.ts (mocked geolocation -> throttled invoke calls; 60s no-send -> banner state + one vibrate) pass.

work_items.title: Offline transition queue: IndexedDB (idb), ordered replay, idempotency keys, exactly-once
work_items.goal: IndexedDB queue for arrive/start/complete/no-show-cancel with X-Idempotency-Key generated at ENQUEUE time (the exactly-once linchpin), ordered FIFO replay on reconnect, 'ceka na odeslani' indicators, exactly-once via server idempotency (A-idem). Accept/decline are never queued. App-level queue via idb, explicitly NOT workbox-background-sync (keeps it fake-indexeddb-testable and working with the SW disabled in E2E).
acceptance_criteria: package.json adds idb@8.0.3 (pure JS, no engine restriction) and a devDependency fake-indexeddb@6.2.5 (engines >=18, satisfied by Node 20.0.0); the queue is an app-level IndexedDB store via idb, explicitly NOT workbox-background-sync.

arrive/start/complete/no-show-cancel are queued when offline (or always routed through the queue) with an X-Idempotency-Key minted at ENQUEUE time and preserved across every retry (the exactly-once linchpin); accept/decline are never queued.

On reconnect the queue replays in FIFO order; each queued item shows a 'ceka na odeslani' indicator; a replay 409 (Idempotency.KeyReused or a state 409) drops that order's queued items and reconciles from GET /orders/{id}; a network error keeps items queued for the next reconnect.
Exactly-once holds: a duplicate replay with the same key gets the server's stored response (A-idem) and the item is dropped.

AC #8 parity green; transitionQueue.test.ts (enqueue/persist/restore across reload via fake-indexeddb; key minted once at enqueue and preserved) and queueReplay.test.ts (FIFO order; retry keeps the same key; 409 drops+reconciles) pass.

work_items.title: Playwright driver specs (mobile viewport): AC#2 full flow, AC#4 decline->New, AC#5 offline queue + decisions/docs
work_items.goal: Mobile-viewport Playwright specs proving AC #2 (start shift -> offer via dispatcher API assign -> accept -> arrive -> start -> complete fixed -> home totals), AC #4 (decline -> order returns to New), and AC #5 (context.setOffline during 'Jsem na miste' -> queued -> delivered exactly once). Reuses the UC-002 harness by adding a mobile Playwright project (leaves Desktop Chrome/dispatcher.spec.ts intact). Records the AC #3 push deferral + UC-003 assumptions in docs/decisions.md; docs/api.md regenerated by the full dotnet test.
acceptance_criteria: playwright.config.ts gains a second project (mobile device e.g. Pixel 5) whose testMatch is scoped to driver.spec.ts; the existing Desktop Chrome project and dispatcher.spec.ts are untouched, and the webServer harness (scripts/e2e-api.mjs: docker db + dotnet run Development Seed__Enabled=true wait /health/ready, then Vite 5173) is reused.

Driver_FullFlow_StartShiftToCompleteFixed_ShowsTotals (AC #2): mobile login as a seeded driver -> select vehicle -> start shift -> dispatcher assigns via API -> offer appears in the foreground within 2 s -> accept -> arrive -> start -> complete with fixed price -> Home shows 1 ride and correct totals.

AC #1 (installability) is verified manually and documented in DEMO.md against a production build (npm run build && npx vite preview -> Chrome DevTools Application panel or Lighthouse PWA category, incl. the maskable-icon check). It is manual because devOptions.enabled:false means the SW and manifest never activate under npm run dev (what the harness boots), so E2E cannot observe them; this is the one binding AC with no automated home and the manual step is its assigned verification.
Driver_Decline_ReturnsOrderToNew (AC #4): decline requires a reason and the order returns to New (dispatcher-visible) within 1 s.

Driver_OfflineArrive_QueuedThenDeliveredExactlyOnce (AC #5): context.setOffline(true) around 'Jsem na miste' queues the action ('ceka na odeslani'), and setOffline(false) delivers it exactly once (a single server-side transition, proven via the X-Idempotency-Key and A-idem).

docs/decisions.md is updated (DoD #6) with the AC #3 push-notification-half deferral to assignment 05 and the UC-003 assumptions echo; docs/api.md is regenerated by the full dotnet test (OpenApi_Document_GeneratesApiMarkdown); DEMO.md documents the manual push test steps and how to boot the harness.

notes: UC-003 = 4 Lane A (api) WIs + 10 Lane B (web) WIs = 14 total. Array is topologically ordered and acyclic. Schema shape matches the UC-002 handoff (per-WI: id, lane [api|web], title, goal, depends_on, estimated_complexity XS/S/M/L/XL, files_touched, rule_citations, required_reads, needs_library_research, acceptance_criteria, verification {tool, filter}). verification.tool enum: dotnet-test | dotnet-build | npm-lint | npm-tsc | vitest | playwright; verification.filter (dotnet-test only) uses single-token FullyQualifiedName~Taxi.Api.Tests.<Area> fragments (the filter charset excludes '/', so vitest/playwright/npm-* tools carry no filter). LANE A is NOT fully parallel: A-offer->A-idem are serialized because they share Common/Orders/OrderService.cs, the six transition endpoints, and Common/ErrorCodes.cs (A-offer edits OrderService's post-commit publish + corrects the IRealtimePublisher XML comment; A-idem then adds the endpoint-level idempotency helper call to the six endpoints and appends the Idempotency.* block to ErrorCodes.cs). A-me and A-geo have empty depends_on and run in parallel with the A-offer->A-idem chain and each other (disjoint files: A-me = new Features/Drivers/GetMySummary + GetMyOrders slices + additive ActiveOrderId on GetMe; A-geo = sole toucher of AuthorizationPolicies.cs + RouteEndpoint.cs). LANE B is a strict chain B-pwa->B-auth->B-home->B-offer->B-ride->B-complete->B-position->B-queue->B-history-settings->B-e2e; B-e2e ADDITIONALLY depends on all of A-offer/A-idem/A-me/A-geo for build-integrity (the Playwright harness boots the API from the shared working tree via dotnet run, which fails to compile if any Lane A WI is mid-implementation) — the vitest-only B WIs need no cross-lane edges because their API calls are mocked. Staging discipline (autonomous single tree): Lane A stages api/ only, Lane B stages web/ only (plus docs/ from B-e2e); neither commits. KEY DECISIONS: (offer expiry consistency) ApplyAssign AND ApplyReassign both set AssignedAt=now (verified OrderStateMachine.cs 130/226), and OfferTimeoutJob expires from AssignedAt+OfferTimeoutSeconds, so A-offer computes expiresAt=AssignedAt+timeout — same instant for job and driver countdown, reassign refreshes the window, no early-timeout bug; NOT a fresh GetUtcNow(). OfferTimeoutSeconds loaded with the mandatory (int?)-cast + ??45 fallback (CLAUDE.md). (idempotency hook) endpoint-level helper in Common/Idempotency — zero FastEndpoints pre/post-processor precedent exists and a post-processor cannot cleanly capture the serialized body; six call sites. IdempotencyRecord is NOT ITenantEntity (UserId-scoped, mirrors RefreshToken/SmsCode / decisions.md assumption 4) so no query filter and no SaveChanges tenant guard. Claim-then-execute four branches: (1) unique-index (UserId,Key) INSERT committed before execution = the lock; (2) stored response -> replay verbatim; (3) in-flight (<60s, null response) -> 409 Idempotency.InFlight retryable; (4) orphaned claim (>=60s, null response, crash between claim and store) -> take over + re-execute (without branch 4 one 500 permanently bricks a queued transition and AC#5 fails in the field). RequestHash mismatch -> 409 Idempotency.KeyReused. Store only 2xx + expected 4xx/409; never 5xx (retryable). Purge opportunistic DELETE <now-24h on the claim path. Header optional (drivers always send, dispatchers never). (A-me date binding) date bound as string? + DateOnly.TryParseExact InvariantCulture (FastEndpoints locale landmine), Europe/Prague calendar day -> UTC window; GetMe gains ActiveOrderId (additive) as the restore source B-ride AC#6 needs (GetMeResponse had no active-order id); isolation tests cover driver B vs driver A AND cross-tenant. (A-geo) new DispatcherOrDriver policy (Dispatcher+FleetAdmin+Driver) per the DispatcherOrCustomer precedent; suggest stays DispatcherOnly.
